report.verdict: A flat-revenue, hold-flattered quarter. Q3-26 revenue of ₱7,841m (~$124.7m) was unchanged YoY and GGR rose just 0.9% to ₱7.04bn (~$111.9m) only because live mass-table hold jumped 380bps to 32.2%; VIP rolling volume fell another 28% and adjusted segment EBITDA dropped 13% to ₱962m (~$15.3m), a 12.3% margin (-180bps). The sequential rebound from a dire Q2 (₱333m) keeps parent UEC's "2H26 return to IR operating profit" target technically alive, but hold-adjusted GGR was still down ~1% and the cost base grew 2% on flat revenue — this is stabilisation, not recovery.
summary: **Headline: flat revenue, lower profit.** Tiger Resort, Leisure & Entertainment Inc (TRLEI, operator of Okada Manila; FYE 31 Dec; unlisted, 100% owned by TSE-listed Universal Entertainment Corp, 6425) reported preliminary Q3-26 (Jul–Sep) total revenue of ₱7,841m (~$124.7m), essentially unchanged YoY (Gaming Intelligence calls it a 'marginal improvement'), with casino GGR +0.9% to ₱7.04bn (~$111.9m) and adjusted segment EBITDA -13.0% to ₱962m (~$15.3m). There is no sell-side consensus for the unlisted entity; the release is unaudited and precedes UEC's consolidated Q3 (expected mid-Nov).

**Mix shift is the whole story.** Mass-table GGR +19.7% to ₱3,010m (~$47.9m) more than offset VIP -21.4% to ₱1,150m (~$18.3m), gaming machines -4.0% to ₱2,880m (~$45.8m) and non-gaming -6.9% to ₱804m (~$12.8m). VIP is now 16.3% of GGR (Q3-25: 20.9%; FY23: ~35% per Fitch); mass tables 42.8%, machines 40.9%.

**Luck did the heavy lifting on mass.** Live mass-table hold was 32.2% vs 28.4% a year ago (+380bps); at the prior-year hold, mass revenue would have been ~₱2.62bn, i.e. ~₱390m lower (estimate). Mass drop grew a more modest +5.4% to ₱9.01bn (~$143m).

**But slots were unlucky, so net luck was roughly neutral.** Machine win rate fell to 5.1% from 5.7% on handle +5.6% — at prior-year hold machine GGR would have been ~₱340m higher. VIP hold 3.9% vs 3.6% added ~₱90m. Our hold-adjusted GGR is ~₱6.90bn, -1.2% YoY (estimate) — the 'return to growth' is a rounding event, not a trend break.

**VIP remains in structural retreat.** Rolling chip volume -27.7% to ₱29.4bn (~$468m), after -22.5% in Q2 (when average VIP tables were cut to 73 from 87). 9M-26 VIP GGR -35.1% to ₱3.59bn (~$57.1m). The POGO ban and weak Korean/Chinese visitation are not reversing.

**Sequential recovery from a trough quarter.** GGR +16.1% QoQ (Q2-26: ₱6.06bn) and adj. EBITDA ~2.9x Q2's ₱333m (~$5.3m); margin +750bps QoQ to 12.3%. Mass-table GGR +36.7% QoQ, VIP +15% QoQ, machines +0.7% QoQ.

**Cost base is rising on flat revenue.** Revenue less adj. EBITDA (opex incl. PAGCOR licence fees and promotional spend) was ₱6,879m, +2.2% YoY (~+₱144m) — consistent with UEC's May warning that customer-acquisition costs are rising amid 'more intense' Manila competition and its August reference to 'strategic investments'. All of the EBITDA decline is cost, not revenue.

**Footfall up, spend per head down.** Visitors +11.8% to 1.45m, hotel occupancy 95.0% (+810bps) — but ADR -4.5% to ₱9,473 (~$151), RevPAR +4.4% to ₱9,000 (~$143), and non-gaming revenue fell 6.9%. GGR per visitor was ₱4,853 (~$77), -9.6% YoY (estimate). The pattern (more rooms, cheaper, less cash non-gaming) reads as comp-driven reinvestment in mass/premium-mass.

**Nine-month picture remains poor.** 9M-26 GGR ₱19.56bn (~$311m), -10.6%; total revenue ~₱22.2bn (~$354m), -9.7% (derived); adj. EBITDA just under ₱2.13bn (~$33.9m), -47.4% (GGRAsia; AGB -47.3%); margin ~9.6% vs ~16.4%. Visitors 4.33m (+5.4%).

**Parent target: IR back to operating profit in 2H26 — unchanged, marginally on track.** With H1-26 results (10 Aug) UEC guided to a 2H26 IR-segment operating profit after an H1 operating loss of ¥1.37bn (~$8.7m) and adj. EBITDA ¥2.74bn (~$17.3m), -62.5%. H1 implies ~¥2bn/quarter of D&A-type charges (~₱0.8bn), so Q3's ₱962m EBITDA points to only a ~₱0.1–0.15bn segment operating profit (estimate) — achieved, but hold-dependent.

**Recovery levers are small or unproven.** UEC's plan: OKADA PLAY online (online mass-table GGR ₱64m vs ₱44m — <1% of GGR), premium-mass acquisition, MICE/large-scale events, Japan/Asia marketing, cost optimisation; Disney-themed hospitality offerings start in Q4-26. Hotel named 'Best Hotel – Manila' at TTG Travel Awards 2026.

**Credit is the binding constraint.** Fitch cut UEC to CCC+ from B- (Jul-26) and on 3 Oct forecast negative FCF in 2026–27 (FCF margin -3.1% / -0.1%), annual EBITDA of ~¥19bn (~$120m) through 2028 versus ~¥20bn (~$127m) needed for cash interest plus capex, EBITDAR fixed-charge cover below 1.5x, and derives bond recovery from Japan operations only because Philippine banks rank senior on the IR assets. S&P moved its outlook to negative in May-26. No significant maturities before Aug-2029.

**Parent group is being carried by pachislot.** UEC H1-26 net sales ¥76.6bn (~$485m, +23.1%), adj. EBITDA ¥15.2bn (~$96m, +148%), net income ¥62m (~$0.4m) vs a ¥9.9bn loss; IR net sales ¥30.13bn (~$191m, -13.0%). Okada Manila is now the group's sole drag.

**Market backdrop is a correction, not a cycle.** PAGCOR's chairman has warned industry GGR could fall up to 19% from 2025's ₱396bn; Philippine GGR fell ~20% in Q2-26; Maybank expects land-based pressure through 2H26 on inflation, utility costs and absent high-rollers; online migration continues. New PAGCOR slot-rebate rules for licensed casinos took effect 14 Oct (headline only; detail unverified).

**Peso at a record low is a translation headwind.** USD/PHP closed ₱62.87 on 14 Oct and breached ₱63 on 15 Oct; UEC's notes are USD-denominated while Okada EBITDA is PHP, shrinking dollar coverage even on flat peso earnings.

**Management emphasis vs. what is buried.** The release leads with visitation +11.8%, 95% occupancy and mass +19.7%; it does not discuss the hold uplift, the 2% opex creep, the ADR cut or the trajectory of VIP table count. Fitch's framing — mass growth 'insufficient to offset' structural VIP decline — is the more honest read.

**Thesis read-through.** Volume indicators (mass drop +5.4%, machine handle +5.6%, visitors +12%) say the mass floor has stabilised; profit indicators (EBITDA -13% on flat revenue, 9M margin ~9.6%) say the property is paying for that stability. Annualised Q3 EBITDA (~₱3.8bn / ~$61m) is below what the parent needs from the IR to be cash-neutral; the burden stays on pachislot and, ultimately, the 2029 refinancing window.
**Share price.** TRLEI is unlisted; the move in parent UEC (6425) on 14–15 Oct could not be verified from the sources read [unverified].

segments.name: Gaming — Okada Manila casino floor (VIP / Mass tables / Gaming machines)
segments.headline: GGR +0.9% to ₱7.04bn (~$111.9m) on a 380bps mass-hold tailwind; hold-adjusted GGR ~-1%; VIP volume -28%.
narrative: They reported casino GGR of ₱7,037m (~$111.9m) for the September quarter, up 0.9% YoY and 16.1% QoQ, which the parent presents as a stabilisation after four consecutive double-digit declines (Q4-25 -34%, Q1-26 -17.2%, Q2-26 -14.6%). The composition matters more than the headline. Mass-market tables generated ₱3,010m (~$47.9m), +19.7% YoY and +36.7% QoQ, on mass drop of ₱9,010m (~$143.3m), +5.4%, and a live-table win rate of 32.2% against 28.4% a year earlier. Live mass revenue rose 19.2% and online mass tables via OKADA PLAY contributed ₱64m (~$1.0m) versus ₱44m, so the online channel is still under 1% of GGR. Stripping the hold uplift — at a 28.4% live hold the mass line would have been roughly ₱2.62bn, +4.5% YoY and in line with drop growth — the underlying mass business is growing mid-single digits, which is respectable in a Philippine market running ~20% down but nowhere near the headline.

VIP continued to shrink. VIP table GGR was ₱1,150m (~$18.3m), -21.4% YoY, on rolling chip volume of ₱29,410m (~$467.8m), -27.7% YoY and a further ~28% below Q2's ₱40.6bn (~$646m); the win rate of 3.9% (vs 3.6%) cushioned the revenue line by ~₱90m. The decline followed a Q2 in which VIP win more than halved (-56%) and the average VIP table count was cut to 73 from 87; the Q3 release does not disclose the table count, which we read as a deliberate omission. VIP is now 16.3% of GGR versus 20.9% a year ago and ~35% in 2023 (Fitch), and for 9M-26 VIP GGR is ₱3.59bn (~$57.1m), -35.1%. With the POGO sector banned and Korean and mainland Chinese visitation still depressed, we see no catalyst for the rolling business and treat its decline as structural; the relevant question is whether Okada keeps shrinking the VIP footprint and redeploys the space to premium mass.

Gaming machines delivered ₱2,880m (~$45.8m), -4.0% YoY but +0.7% QoQ, on handle that rose 5.6% while the win rate fell to 5.1% from 5.7%. At the prior-year win rate machine GGR would have been ~₱3.22bn, up ~7%; implied handle of roughly ₱56bn (~$0.9bn) is a genuine volume positive. Whether the 60bps hold decline is variance or a structural loosening (free-play, promotional reinvestment, and the new PAGCOR slot-rebate rules that took effect on 14 October) is the key open question for Q4, because machines are 41% of GGR and the single largest profit pool on the floor. Combining the three products, our luck-adjusted GGR is ~₱6.90bn, -1.2% YoY: the favourable mass hold and the unfavourable machine hold broadly cancel, leaving the mix shift from VIP to mass as the real underlying story.

The P&L consequence is that revenue was flat while adjusted segment EBITDA fell 13.0% to ₱962m (~$15.3m), a 12.3% margin, -180bps YoY but +750bps QoQ from the 4.8% trough in Q2. Revenue less EBITDA — which captures PAGCOR licence fees, promotional allowances, labour and marketing — rose 2.2% to ₱6,879m (~$109.4m). UEC had flagged in May that competition among Manila operators was 'more intense' and that customer-acquisition costs were rising, and in August that Q2 expenses included 'strategic investments'; Q3 shows that spend persisting. Management has not disclosed promotional cost as a percentage of drop or handle, and we would want that metric before accepting that the mass-volume growth is margin-accretive rather than bought. For 9M-26 GGR is ₱19.56bn (~$311m), -10.6%, and adjusted EBITDA just under ₱2.13bn (~$33.9m), -47.4%, so Q3's ₱962m represents 45% of year-to-date profit. There is no numeric segment guidance; UEC's stated objective is an IR-segment operating profit in 2H26 through online expansion, premium-mass acquisition, Japan/Asia marketing and cost optimisation, and Q3's EBITDA covers the ~₱0.8bn/quarter of depreciation-type charges implied by H1 with only ~₱0.1–0.15bn to spare (our estimate).

segments.name: Non-gaming, hotel & visitation
segments.headline: Visitors +11.8% and occupancy 95%, but ADR -4.5% and non-gaming revenue -6.9% to ₱804m (~$12.8m) — comps, not cash.
narrative: They welcomed approximately 1.45 million visitors in the quarter, up 11.8% from 1.30 million, and ran the 993-room hotel at 95.0% occupancy against 86.9% a year earlier and 91.4% in Q2. The headline is strong and the parent leads with it, but the yield metrics tell the other half: average daily rate fell 4.5% to ₱9,473 (~$151) and RevPAR rose only 4.4% to ₱9,000 (~$143), down from ₱9,242 (~$147) in Q2. Non-gaming revenue — hotel, F&B, retail and entertainment — declined 6.9% YoY and 13.4% QoQ to ₱804m (~$12.8m), 10.3% of total revenue versus 11.0% a year ago and 13.3% in Q2. A property cannot fill 8 points more rooms, cut rate and still see cash non-gaming fall unless a larger share of the incremental occupancy is complimentary, which is consistent with the mass-reinvestment push visible on the gaming floor. We would therefore read the occupancy figure as a marketing input rather than a hospitality output.

Spend per visitor is deteriorating. GGR per visitor was ~₱4,853 (~$77), -9.6% YoY (Q3-25: ~₱5,369), and total revenue per visitor ~₱5,408 (~$86), -10.5%; on a nine-month basis GGR per visitor is ~₱4,517, -15% (all analyst-derived). Some of this is the arithmetic of losing high-value VIP players while adding low-value foot traffic from events, but it also underlines that incremental visitation is being bought at lower yield. Management points to large-scale events as a non-gaming growth lever and in August said it had 'intensified' efforts to expand non-gaming revenue via such events; the Q3 numbers do not yet show it. For 9M-26 non-gaming revenue is ₱2,680m (~$42.6m), -2.2%, on visitation of 4.33 million, +5.4%.

The forward catalysts are Disney-themed hospitality offerings launching from Q4-26, continued MICE promotion, and the TTG Travel Awards 2026 'Best Hotel – Manila' recognition that President and COO Nobuki Sato highlighted. None of these is quantified, and with the peso at a record low (₱63/$ on 15 October) inbound tourism economics improve at the margin for Korean and Japanese visitors, which is the main source-market upside to watch. We would want Q4 to show RevPAR growth with stable or rising ADR and non-gaming revenue tracking occupancy before crediting the hotel with a genuine turn.

segments.name: Parent context — Universal Entertainment Corp (TSE: 6425): IR segment & credit
segments.headline: Group profit is pachislot-driven; the IR segment lost ¥1.37bn (~$8.7m) in H1-26 and Fitch (CCC+) sees negative FCF through 2027.
narrative: UEC consolidates Okada Manila as its Integrated Resort segment and reports in yen, so the TRLEI peso release is the leading indicator for the segment print due in mid-November. For H1-26 (Jan–Jun; UEC's 'second quarter' is cumulative) IR net sales were ¥30.13bn (~$191m), -13.0% YoY, the operating loss widened slightly to ¥1.37bn (~$8.7m) from ¥1.32bn, and adjusted EBITDA fell 62.5% to ¥2.74bn (~$17.3m). The group nonetheless swung to net income attributable to owners of ¥62m (~$0.4m) from a ¥9.87bn loss, on net sales of ¥76.6bn (~$485m), +23.1%, adjusted EBITDA of ¥15.2bn (~$96m), +148%, and segment operating profit of ¥14.2bn (~$90m), +174% — all of it the Japanese pachinko/pachislot recovery. Management's stated intent is to return the IR segment to operating profit in 2H26 by expanding online gaming (OKADA PLAY), attracting premium-mass customers, strengthening marketing in Japan and across Asia, hosting large-scale events and 'promoting cost optimization and prioritizing the allocation of management resources'. The Q3 TRLEI numbers suggest that target is being met by a thin margin and with help from hold.

The credit picture frames everything. Fitch downgraded UEC's IDR to CCC+ from B- in July 2026, citing the 'material deterioration' in the IR segment, and on 3 October laid out a rating case of subdued EBITDA and negative free cash flow in 2026 and 2027 (FCF margins of -3.1% and -0.1%), annual EBITDA of about ¥19bn (~$120m) through 2028 against roughly ¥20bn (~$127m) required to cover cash interest and capex, and EBITDAR fixed-charge coverage at or below 1.5x through 2027. Critically, Fitch now derives recovery for the USD senior notes from post-restructuring Japanese cash flows only, because offshore bondholders may struggle to access the Philippine IR assets on which local banks hold senior claims. S&P revised its outlook on UEC to negative in May 2026 on stiff Philippine competition. The group has no significant debt maturities before August 2029, which buys time but not optionality: with the peso at a record low against the dollar and Okada EBITDA in pesos, dollar coverage erodes even on flat local-currency earnings.

Our read is that Okada Manila does not need to grow to satisfy the parent's near-term objectives — it needs to stop consuming cash. Annualising Q3's ₱962m gives ~₱3.8bn (~$61m, ~¥9.7bn) of IR EBITDA, roughly half of the group total Fitch models and insufficient to cover the IR's own share of group interest. The swing factors into 2027 are (i) whether the mass floor can hold Q3 volumes at normal hold without further promotional escalation, (ii) whether UEC monetises or restructures anything at the IR level, and (iii) whether pachislot demand holds up long enough to carry the refinancing conversation into 2028.

Swing factor (i): whether the mass floor holds Q3 volumes at normal hold without further promotional escalation.
Swing factor (ii): whether UEC monetises or restructures anything at the IR level.
Swing factor (iii): whether pachislot demand holds long enough to carry the refinancing conversation into 2028.

highlights.text: Mass-floor volumes are genuinely growing: mass table drop +5.4% to ₱9.01bn (~$143m), machine handle +5.6%, visitors +11.8% to 1.45m — in a Philippine market running ~20% down. Hold-adjusted mass GGR ~+4–5%.

Sharp sequential recovery from the Q2 trough: GGR +16.1% QoQ, adj. EBITDA ₱962m (~$15.3m) vs ₱333m (~$5.3m), margin 12.3% vs 4.8% — enough to put UEC's 2H26 IR operating-profit target narrowly on track (est. ~₱0.1–0.15bn Q3 segment EBIT).

Live mass-table hold of 32.2% (+380bps) added ~₱390m to mass GGR — a windfall, but one that partly offset an unlucky 5.1% machine hold (-60bps, ~-₱340m), so the reported GGR is not far from luck-neutral.
Hotel metrics at record levels: 95.0% occupancy (+810bps), RevPAR +4.4% to ₱9,000 (~$143); 'Best Hotel – Manila' TTG award; Disney-themed offerings launch in Q4-26.
Online mass tables (OKADA PLAY) grew ~45% to ₱64m (~$1.0m) — tiny, but the only channel with structural growth in a market migrating online.
Parent is self-funding for now: UEC H1-26 adj. EBITDA ¥15.2bn (~$96m, +148%) on pachislot strength; no significant maturities before Aug-2029.

lowlights.text: VIP keeps collapsing: rolling volume -27.7% to ₱29.4bn (~$468m) after -22.5% in Q2; 9M VIP GGR -35.1% to ₱3.59bn (~$57.1m); VIP share of GGR 16.3% vs ~35% in 2023. No catalyst for reversal (POGO ban, Korean/Chinese visitation).

Profit fell on flat revenue: adj. EBITDA -13% to ₱962m (~$15.3m) with opex (revenue less EBITDA) +2.2% to ₱6,879m (~$109m) — the cost of acquiring mass volume in an intensifying Entertainment City market. Promo % of drop/handle is not disclosed.
Hold-adjusted GGR ~₱6.90bn, -1.2% YoY (estimate): the 'return to growth' headline is a rounding outcome, and Q4 faces mean reversion on the 32.2% mass hold.
Non-gaming -6.9% to ₱804m (~$12.8m) and ADR -4.5% despite 95% occupancy — incremental rooms look comped; GGR per visitor -9.6% to ~₱4,853 (~$77).

Credit deterioration: Fitch CCC+ (from B-), negative FCF 2026–27, EBITDAR fixed-charge cover <1.5x, EBITDA ~¥19bn vs ~¥20bn of interest + capex; bond recovery now assessed on Japan assets only. S&P outlook negative.
9M-26 adj. EBITDA -47.4% to ~₱2.13bn (~$33.9m), margin ~9.6% vs ~16.4%; annualised Q3 run-rate (~₱3.8bn) is far below the ₱5bn+ the property generated in FY25's first nine months alone.

Peso at record low (₱62.87 on 14 Oct, >₱63 on 15 Oct) shrinks USD-equivalent EBITDA against USD-denominated parent notes; new PAGCOR slot-rebate rules (14 Oct) are an unquantified margin risk on 41% of GGR.

forecast.intro: TRLEI gives no numeric guidance and UEC has not changed its only stated target: with H1-26 results on 10 Aug it committed to returning the IR segment to operating profit in 2H26 (after an H1 operating loss of ¥1.37bn / ~$8.7m), via OKADA PLAY online, premium-mass acquisition, Japan/Asia marketing, large-scale events and cost optimisation. Q3 is the first data point and it is the IR segment alone that determines whether the target is met — pachislot is already carrying the group. The EBITDA bridge below shows that the YoY decline is entirely cost: revenue was flat because a ~₱500m mass-table gain (of which ~₱390m was hold) offset ~₱490m of VIP, machine and non-gaming erosion, while the cost base rose ~₱144m.

bridge.title: Revenue mix: mass +₱500m (hold ~+₱390m) vs VIP -₱310m, machines -₱120m, non-gaming -₱60m
Opex incl. PAGCOR fees, promo & marketing (derived)

forecast.view: **Q4-26E (analyst estimate):** the comp is easy (Q4-25 GGR ₱5.93bn, -34% YoY, the cycle low) and seasonality helps, but we assume live mass hold reverts toward 28–30% and machine hold toward 5.3–5.5%. On mass drop ~+5%, machine handle ~+5% and VIP volume -20–25% we model GGR of **₱6.4–6.9bn (~$102–110m), +8–16% YoY**, total revenue ~₱7.2–7.7bn, and adj. EBITDA of **₱650–900m (~$10–14m)** at a 9–12% margin — meaning 2H26 segment operating profit is achievable only at the top of that range once ~₱0.8bn/quarter of D&A-type charges are deducted. **FY26E:** GGR ~₱26.0–26.5bn (~$413–421m), -5% to -7% vs FY25's ₱27.8bn; adj. EBITDA ~₱2.8–3.0bn (~$45–48m), roughly -45% to -50% on the 9M trend (FY25 full-year EBITDA not verified). **Margin direction:** flat-to-down until promotional intensity is disclosed and contained; we would not underwrite the Q3 12.3% as a run-rate. **Leverage direction:** up at the parent — Fitch models EBITDA ~¥19bn vs ~¥20bn of cash interest plus capex and negative FCF in both 2026 and 2027, so net debt rises even with no maturities before Aug-2029; a weaker peso compounds USD coverage. **Swing factors:** (1) mass hold normalisation (±₱300–400m/quarter of GGR); (2) machine hold under the new PAGCOR slot-rebate rules; (3) whether VIP table count is cut further and floor space redeployed; (4) Disney-themed Q4 launch and event calendar for non-gaming yield; (5) any IR-level asset or capital-structure action by UEC.
watch: Q4-26 live mass hold vs the 32.2% Q3 print and mass drop growth — the test of whether volume survives normal luck.
Machine win rate under PAGCOR's slot-rebate rules effective 14 Oct 2026; machines are 41% of GGR.
Promotional reinvestment: opex per visitor and non-gaming revenue vs occupancy — Q3 showed 95% occupancy with ADR -4.5% and non-gaming -6.9%.
VIP rolling volume (₱29.4bn in Q3) and average VIP table count (last disclosed 73 in Q2-26 vs 87).
UEC consolidated Q3 (mid-Nov) — IR segment operating result vs the 2H26 operating-profit commitment; any revision to FY26 forecasts.
Fitch (CCC+) / S&P (negative outlook) actions and USD/PHP (record low ₱63+) against USD senior notes due Aug-2029.
OKADA PLAY online scaling beyond ₱64m/quarter and the Q4-26 Disney-themed hospitality launch.
Philippine market data: PAGCOR GGR run-rate vs the chairman's up-to-19% FY decline warning; Entertainment City competitive intensity and Casino Filipino privatisation.

The UEC/TRLEI preliminary Q3-26 PDF could not be retrieved directly (web-fetch budget exhausted); every Q3-26 figure was triangulated across four independent outlets (GGRAsia, Asia Gaming Brief, Inside Asian Gaming, Focus Gaming News) that each cite the 14 Oct 2026 filing, and they agree on all headline numbers (one minor discrepancy: 9M adj. EBITDA -47.4% per GGRAsia vs -47.3% per AGB; GGR quoted as $111.8m vs $112m on rounding). Q3-25, Q1-26 and Q2-26 comparatives come from the same outlets' contemporaneous reports on the TRLEI filings. Items explicitly derived or estimated by the analyst and labelled as such: Q2-26 total revenue and product split, 9M-26 mass/machine GGR, machine handle, Q3-25 drop/RCV, hold-normalised GGR, GGR per visitor, implied D&A and segment EBIT, all forward estimates. Not verified: UEC share-price reaction, the principal amount/coupon of the 2029 notes, TRLEI net income/cash/debt (not in the preliminary release), FY25 full-year adj. EBITDA, and the content of the PAGCOR slot-rebate rules (headline only).
